rawOutput.title: Use the Product Rule Independently
rawOutput.rationale: This four-session problem-solving plan begins with the meaning and structure of the product rule, then uses a complete worked example before guided and independent practice. Each session fits a 15-minute window and keeps one action prominent. Later sessions retrieve and apply the rule with less support.

sessions.title: Understand the Product Rule
sessions.objective: Recognize when a derivative requires the product rule and explain its structure.
sessions.amountLabel: One product-rule model with one recognition check
contentTargets: The formula (fg)' = f'g + fg' and why both terms are necessary
completionEvidence: Explain what changes and what stays unchanged in each term of the product rule
Classify one expression as requiring or not requiring the product rule

sessions.title: Follow the Product-Rule Procedure
sessions.objective: Apply the product rule to a complete worked example using the power rule.
sessions.amountLabel: One worked polynomial-product example and one guided problem
contentTargets: A step-by-step procedure for differentiating a product of two polynomial functions
completionEvidence: Apply the product-rule procedure to one guided polynomial product
Explain where each part of the resulting derivative came from

sessions.title: Retrieve and Apply the Rule
sessions.objective: Use the product rule from memory on a similar problem with limited help.
sessions.amountLabel: One unsupported product-rule problem with one correction pass
contentTargets: Independent setup and differentiation of a polynomial product
completionEvidence: Recall the product rule without looking
Solve one product-rule derivative and correct any identified error

sessions.title: Choose and Use the Rule Independently
sessions.objective: Decide whether the product rule is needed and apply it accurately without guidance.
sessions.amountLabel: Two mixed derivative problems: one product and one non-product
contentTargets: Rule selection and independent differentiation in a small mixed set
completionEvidence: Classify two derivative problems by whether they require the product rule
Solve both derivatives and justify the chosen rule

methodBriefing.name: Feynman Technique
methodBriefing.what: Study an accurate model, explain it in plain language, repair the comparison, and explain it again without copying.
methodBriefing.why: Connecting steps and causes helps expose gaps and build a more usable mental model.
how: Read or view the model once.
Explain the idea in your own words.
Compare your explanation with the model and repair any gap.
Explain it again after repair without copying.
methodBriefing.completion: A complete explanation states the rule and why both terms are needed.
personalization: Use one visible step at a time.
Start with the big picture before details.
Use the concrete example as the anchor for your explanation.

activities.label: model
activities.title: Product rule structure
activities.body: Review the model and focus on how the two terms work. Then move on to your own explanation.

essentialIdeas: The product rule says (fg)' = f'g + fg', so differentiating a product needs one term for each factor changing while the other stays in place.

activities.label: explain
activities.title: Explain it in your own words
activities.body: Write a short explanation of why the rule has two terms. Keep it in plain language.
activities.concept: The product rule says (fg)' = f'g + fg', so differentiating a product needs one term for each factor changing while the
activities.correctAnswer: One factor changes while the other stays the same, and then the roles switch, so both terms are needed.
activities.feedback: A complete answer names both changing cases and why one term alone is not enough. If you only say the rule, add the reason behind each term.

activities.label: repair
activities.title: Fix the missing term
activities.body: Revise your explanation if it left out one changing factor. Make the two cases explicit.
activities.misconceptionSummary: Thinking only one factor gets differentiated while the other stays fixed, so a product has just one derivative term.
activities.concept: The product rule says (fg)' = f'g + fg', so differentiating a product needs one term for each factor changing while the
activities.correctAnswer: Both factors must get a turn changing, so the derivative has two terms: one for f changing and one for g changing.
activities.feedback: This repairs the missing second case. The corrected explanation should say what changes in each term and why both are needed.

activities.label: reexplain
activities.title: Explain it again
activities.body: Explain the rule again in plain language, without copying the model. Keep it short and clear.
activities.concept: The product rule says (fg)' = f'g + fg', so differentiating a product needs one term for each factor changing while the
activities.correctAnswer: The derivative of a product needs two parts: one where the first factor changes and one where the second factor changes.
activities.feedback: A strong reexplanation gives the rule and the reason in your own words. It should make clear that each factor gets one changing case.

activities.label: check
activities.title: Which rule fits?
activities.body: Choose the correct rule for this expression. Then answer in one sentence.
activities.feedback: A product of two functions uses the product rule because both factors can change. The other rules fit different structures.
